description: Explicit founding and dissolution dates for political parties. These are asserted facts about the organisations, NOT inferred from their presence or absence in election results. The party registry at data/browse/details/parties/ carries firstYear/lastYear, but those are exactly the min and max year of each party's linked elections (verified 185/185) and are therefore a summary of contest history, not a lifespan.

conventions.founded: ISO date. Use `foundedPrecision` to say how much of it is real.
conventions.foundedPrecision: day | month | year — a party known only to a year is recorded as YYYY-01-01 with precision 'year', never as a false exact date.
conventions.dissolved: ISO date, or null. Null is only meaningful in combination with `status`.
conventions.status: active | dissolved | unknown. This is the field that removes the ambiguity in the derived lastYear: 'active' means the party still exists and a null `dissolved` is a positive fact; 'unknown' means no dissolution date is recorded and none should be inferred; 'dissolved' requires a date. A party that stopped contesting is NOT thereby dissolved, and a party whose label appears after its dissolution is not thereby still alive.
conventions.partyStrings: Exact `party` values in the election data that belong to this organisation. Either a plain string, or an object {string, bodies} restricting it to certain bodySlug values. A string MAY be claimed by more than one party when their date windows are disjoint — that is how a succession is modelled, and the date then decides which organisation a candidacy belongs to.
conventions.window: Membership is the half-open interval [founded, dissolved). A candidacy dated exactly on the dissolution date belongs to the SUCCESSOR, not the dissolved party, so that a same-day handover has no gap and no overlap.
conventions.corruptedStrings: Party strings that are data defects but unambiguously belong to this organisation. Kept separate so the defect stays visible rather than being silently normalised away.
conventions.source: Where the dates came from. Required — an uncited lifespan is not usable.
conventions.predecessor / successor: A SUCCESSION: the predecessor ends and the successor begins, same lineage. The two dates must match exactly, and the registry enforces that.
conventions.splitFrom: A SPLIT, which is not a succession: the parent organisation CONTINUES and the child branches off it. No date equality is implied or checked; the registry only requires that the parent existed on the child's founding date. Using predecessor/successor for a split would wrongly assert that the parent ended.
conventions.revivalOf: A REVIVAL: an organisation founded under a name previously used by one that had already dissolved, with a GAP between them. Distinct from a succession, which hands over on the day, and from a split, where the parent continues. The registry requires that the earlier entity was dissolved on or before this one's founding.

parties.name: Ulster Unionist Party
parties.notes: The two corrupted strings are 1989 Ballymoney Town records carrying the candidate's occupation in the party field ('Businssman' is the source's typo).

parties.name: Sinn Féin
parties.notes: Applies to the exact string 'Sinn Féin' only. The distinct strings 'Pro-Treaty Sinn Féin', 'Anti-Treaty Sinn Féin', 'Republican Sinn Féin' and "Sinn Féin Workers'" are separate organisations and are not covered by this entry; whether any of them is continuous with this one is a question this file records no view on.

parties.name: Alliance Party of Northern Ireland
parties.notes: Unrelated strings containing the word Alliance ('Independent Alliance', 'Anti-Austerity Alliance', 'Socialist Environmental Alliance', 'Independent Health Alliance', 'United Left Alliance', 'South Kerry Independent Alliance') are separate organisations and are not matched.

parties.name: Democratic Unionist Party
parties.notes: 'United Loy DUP' (1977 Larne Area A, Samuel J. Martin) is NOT attributed here. It contains the substring DUP but reads as 'United Loyalist', and no evidence in the data settles which organisation it was; it remains unattributed rather than guessed.
parties.foundedNote: 1971-09-30 is the announcement by Paisley and Boal (CAIN chronology 1971; Elliott and Flackes 1999, p. 7); the first meeting, at the Ulster Hall, was 30 October 1971, the party's anniversary date (Elliott and Flackes 1999, p. 7; The Irish Times, 31 October 1996). Kept as the announcement; the rally is a lineage event.

parties.name: United Kingdom Unionist Party
parties.notes: 'UK Unionist Party' is the same organisation under a second string, used only by the local-government dataset (22 candidacies, 1997-2005). Robert McCartney's 1995-06-15 North Down by-election candidacy carries the string 'UKUP' ten months before this founding date and is reported as a contradiction; the party was constituted after that by-election, so the label appears to have been applied retrospectively. Last candidacy is 2007-03-07, eighteen months before dissolution. The Northern Ireland Unionist Party split from the UKUP in 1999 and is recorded separately as niup, with splitFrom pointing here; note the two organisations wound up within six months of each other in 2008 (NIUP 10 March, UKUP 4 September).

parties.name: Northern Ireland Unionist Party
parties.notes: A SPLIT from the UKUP, not a succession: the UKUP continued and contested until 2007, so predecessor/successor would wrongly assert that it ended in 1999. Two strings, both this organisation: 'NI Unionist Party' (4 candidacies, 2001 Westminster and 2003 Assembly) and 'Northern Ireland Unionist Party' (8, 2001 local government). All 12 fall inside the window. The party's last candidacy is 2003-11-26, more than four years before dissolution — a gap that is invisible to the derived lastYear, which would have reported 2003 as the end.

parties.name: People Before Profit
parties.notes: Deliberately NOT scoped by body, unlike the Green entry. The 'PBP' string covers 75 candidacies on NI bodies and 33 in dail-eireann and ireland-european, and People Before Profit organises across both jurisdictions as one party, so both are attributed here. If that is wrong and the two should be separate organisations, this entry needs splitting the way Green (NI) is. 'Solidarity-PBP' (86 candidacies, 2019-2024, dail-eireann and ireland-european only) is NOT included: it is the joint ticket registered with Solidarity, and a joint ticket is its own registration rather than the component party — the same treatment given to UCUNF.

parties.name: Vanguard Unionist Progressive Party
parties.source: CAIN chronologies 1973 (30 March 1973), 1977 (26 November 1977) and 1978 (25 February 1978); Elliott and Flackes 1999, p. 14
parties.notes: Founded 30 March 1973 (CAIN chronology 1973); the Ulster Vanguard movement dates from 9 February 1972. Craig announced on 26 November 1977 that it would cease to be a political party from 25 February 1978; CAIN records the dissolution that day. The earlier 1978-02-20 had no source found. The 1982 candidacies belong to vanguard-1982.

parties.name: Vanguard Unionist Progressive Party
parties.notes: Deliberately carries the SAME `name` as entity vanguard and a different id — the case the id scheme exists for. Shares the party string with its predecessor; the two are separated by their lifespans alone, which are disjoint (1972-02-09..1978-02-20 and 1982-08-30..1987-05-27), so no alias scoping is needed. This claims all three Vanguard candidacies at the 1982-10-20 Assembly election: William Craig (Belfast East), John Dunlop and Robert Overend (both Mid Ulster). Craig's is the only one of the three that is his own; the other two are captured because they carry the same label inside the same window. Narrow the alias to Craig alone if that is not intended. Not a succession — there is a four-and-a-half-year gap after the original dissolved — hence revivalOf rather than predecessor/successor.

parties.name: Ecology Party (Northern Ireland)
parties.source: PROVISIONAL — supplied by repository owner 2026-07-26 as a working value pending confirmation
parties.notes: The founding date is the date of the 1981 local elections, which is when the Ecology label first appears in the data (Malcolm Samuel, Coleraine Area B; Avril McCandless, Coleraine Area C). It is a placeholder for the party's actual founding, not a sourced date, and should be replaced. The dissolution date is the founding of the Green Party, i.e. a same-day handover.

parties.name: Green Party (Northern Ireland)
parties.notes: The 'Green' string is scoped to NI bodies. The same string carries 264 candidacies in dail-eireann and ireland-european which belong to the Green Party in the Republic, a separate organisation with no dates supplied here; those are deliberately left unattributed rather than folded in. 'Green / Ecology' is a label used only by the local-government dataset, across 1981-2011, and is therefore shared with the predecessor and resolved by date.

parties.name: Progressive Unionist Party
parties.notes: Only the year is known, so the date is recorded as 1977-01-01 with foundedPrecision 'year'. That 01-01 is padding, NOT a claim about the day — the first entry in the registry to use this, and the reason the field exists. Status is 'unknown' rather than 'active': no dissolution date was supplied and none is inferred, though the party's most recent candidacy is 2023. Claims only the string 'PUP'; the ten 1938 Stormont candidacies labelled 'Progressive Unionist' are a different organisation, entity progressive-unionist-1938. One 1973 candidacy (Elizabeth Roulton, Ballymena Area C, 107 votes) falls four years before this founding and is reported as a contradiction.

parties.name: NI21
parties.notes: The only entry so far with a dissolution date, and therefore the only one where the founded/dissolved window can actually exclude a candidacy.

parties.name: Communist Party of Ireland
parties.source: For Unity and Socialism (manifesto of the special congress, Belfast, 15 March 1970), Irish Left Archive; Elliott and Flackes 1999, p. 4 (14 March 1970)
parties.notes: The party formed in 1970 by the merger of the Irish Workers' Party and the Communist Party of Northern Ireland. Wikidata's 1933 inception is the earlier Communist Party of Ireland (split 1941).
